sections.html:
Alabama's southwestern corner belongs to Mobile County, the state's third most populous, with 414,809 residents at the last full count. Mobile is the seat and the biggest city. Shoreline is everywhere, including Dauphin Island, Gaillard Island and Mon Louis Island, and that shapes insurance, flood maps and what a house is worth.

The county has 163,750 households and 184,441 housing units, 11.2% of them vacant. Owners live in 64.6% of occupied homes, and 35.4% are rented. Landlords make up a large share of sellers, and some of those rentals carry arrears.

Nine cities lie inside the county: Bayou La Batre, Chickasaw, Citronelle, Creola, Mobile, Prichard, Saraland, Satsuma and Semmes. Dauphin Island and Mount Vernon are towns. Communities such as Theodore, Grand Bay, Tillmans Corner, Axis, Chunchula and Wilmer have no city government. A house in Saraland, one in Theodore and one on Dauphin Island all sit in one county, but the millage and school levy on each can differ, so confirm the taxing districts for your parcel before trusting an online estimate.

The Mobile County Revenue Commission assesses and collects property tax for the county. Its offices are closed on Wednesdays, a fact that catches people out near year end when lines are longest.

For a home, the Revenue Commission handles assessment and billing, and the county probate office records the deed. Keep those two straight when you sell.

Owners of rental houses with appliances or furnishings, or a business that keeps equipment at a house, also face a personal property rule. Personal property must be listed after October 1 and no later than December 31. Listing after the third Monday in January adds a 10% penalty plus fees.

Tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. After that the state timetable takes over.

MonthStep in the state timetable
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

An owner who knows a bill is unpaid has until December 31 to clear it before the delinquency process starts. If you plan to sell, the best time to act is before January.

The climate is mild and humid, and a 2007 study named Mobile the wettest city in the contiguous 48 states, with 66.3 inches of average annual rainfall. A buyer or inspector looks at water first, so roofs, drainage, crawl spaces and flood zones carry more weight here than in most places.

Frederic, a Category 3 storm, passed over Mobile on September 12, 1979. Ivan struck on September 16, 2004, and Katrina on August 29, 2005 brought an 11.45 foot surge that flooded downtown and the Battleship Parkway. Sally in 2020 was the first hurricane since Ivan to hit Alabama directly, and Zeta followed a month later as a Category 3.

Eastern sections of Mobile that flooded during Katrina and houses with storm damage that was only partly repaired are the properties that stall in a retail sale. A cash buyer will take them in their current condition.

An appeal begins with a written challenge to the valuation through the county Board of Equalization, and a ruling from that board can go to circuit court within 30 days. Alabama Code 40-3-25 requires notice to the board secretary and the circuit clerk, plus a bond, and the taxpayer must pay the prior year's tax before it becomes delinquent or risk dismissal.

At closing, a title company or closing attorney normally collects the payoff for any unpaid tax from the seller's proceeds. The deed goes to the probate court for recording, and Alabama Code 40-22-1 sets the deed tax at $0.50 for each $500 of value.

  • Get a current balance from the Revenue Commission before you list or accept an offer.
  • Check the parcel for exemptions that need to be released or reclaimed.
  • Gather the paperwork for any inherited property, since the deed chain must be clean.
  • Ask the title company how it will handle a lien from an earlier year.

Sellers across the county tend to own storm-worn roofs, older housing or an estate. Many are in the historic neighborhoods of Mobile, including Ashland Place, Oakleigh Garden, Old Dauphin Way and Spring Hill, where older houses need more upkeep than newer ones. Some own houses in areas hit by past storms. Others inherited a house and cannot afford the repairs and back tax at once.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in Mobile County as is, including those with tax due, so the seller does not pay for repairs before closing. The title company takes any unpaid property tax from the proceeds.

A mortgage-backed sale asks a lot of the house: an appraisal, a lender inspection and often an insurance check. In a county this wet, those steps are where problems surface, from a worn roof to a wet crawl space. Each one can bring a demand for repairs or a lower price.

A cash sale removes those steps. The buyer looks at the house as it stands, and the offer already reflects its condition. That is useful for owners facing a deadline, such as a tax sale in May, a move or an estate that must be settled.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
First, learn the balance. Phone the Revenue Commission on any day except Wednesday and ask what is owed and whether an earlier year is open. Second, gather the deed and any papers about an estate. Third, ask a cash buyer for a written offer and compare the net you would receive after the tax payoff.

Fourth, choose a closing date that leaves room for the title search. The title company confirms who holds title, requests the payoff, drafts the settlement statement and arranges recording of the deed. You sign once, the tax is paid from the proceeds, and the rest is yours.

If a landlord owns the house, add the leases to the folder and decide whether tenants stay or go. A buyer will want to know before the offer is final.

faqs.q: When is Mobile County property tax due?
faqs.a: Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. The Mobile County Revenue Commission collects it.

faqs.q: Is the Mobile County Revenue Commission open on Wednesdays?
faqs.a: No. All of its offices are closed on Wednesdays, so plan visits for other weekdays.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Mobile County property tax?
faqs.a: After December 31 the bill is delinquent. The state timetable then sends it to probate court in February, advertises it in April, and holds a tax sale in May.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an assessment in Mobile County?
faqs.a: A written appeal goes to the Board of Equalization. An appeal of the board's decision to circuit court must be taken within 30 days under Alabama Code 40-3-25.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mobile County house that has back property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the back tax from the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the Revenue Commission for a balance first.
